english.title: Sponsor fail give written notice of urgent safety measures of pandemic disease / serious risk to human health

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Medicines for Human Use Clinical Trials Regulations 2004

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being the sponsor of a clinical trial for which urgent safety measures were taken in order to protect the participants of the trial against an immediate hazard to their health or safety, failed to give written notice to the licensing authority, namely **(..SPECIFY THE LICENSING AUTHORITY..) and the relevant ethics committee, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ETHICS COMMITTEE..) of the measures taken and the circumstances giving rise to those measures in respect of a disease which was pandemic and a serious risk to human health or potentially a serious risk to human health, as soon as possible
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 30(2)(a), 49(1)(f) and 52 of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location

english.notes:
(i) Regulation 51 of the of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004 provides a defence of due diligence.
(ii) This offence should not be used after the 27th April 2026 due to changes made by the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) (Amendment) Regulations 2025. For the offence applicable after this date, see H15919.
